content: Sodium propionate, also known as sodium propanoate, is the sodium salt derived from propionic acid. Its chemical formula is Na(C2H5COO). This compound appears as a white crystalline solid and has the property of being deliquescent, meaning it absorbs moisture from the air under humid conditions. Sodium propionate is synthesized through a chemical reaction between propionic acid and either sodium carbonate or sodium hydroxide. This compound is widely utilized as a food preservative. In the European Union, it is labeled with the E number E281 and is primarily employed as a mold inhibitor in bakery products. Sodium propionate has been approved for use as a food additive in several regions, including the European Union, the United States, Australia, and New Zealand. In Australia and New Zealand, it is identified by its International Numbering System (INS) code, 281.
